newsitem.title: FRANCE: Pons sees French 1997 growth near 2.4-2.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Pons sees French 1997 growth near 2.4-2.5 pct.

text.p: French transport Minister Bernard Pons said on Sunday that economic growth in France would reach 2.4-2.5 percent in 1997.
But he said this may not be enough to substantially boost jobs.

"In 1997 growth will be totally different from growth in 1996. We will have growth of around 2.4-2.5 percent. But this will still not be sufficient to allow for very large job creations," Pons told RTL radio.
French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said earlier this week that economic growth in France and Germany would be about 2.5 percent in 1997.
Arthuis made the forecast after meeting with German Finance Minister Theo Waigel and the central bank heads of France and Germany in Lyon.

In February Arthuis had said he considered the government's official forecast of a 2.3 percent gross domestic product growth for 1997 to be a minimum threshold. French economic growth was 1.3 percent in 1996.
